foods.name: Kanin (white rice, cooked)
foods.source_note: USDA FDC "Rice, white, long-grain, regular, cooked, unenriched" per 100 g.

foods.name: Sinangag (garlic fried rice)
foods.source_note: 400 g USDA cooked white rice + 15 g vegetable oil + 10 g garlic, mixed then scaled to 100 g. Pinch of salt. No soy sauce in this baseline.

foods.name: Chicken adobo
foods.source_note: Per 1 kg chicken: 60 ml soy sauce, 60 ml vinegar, 15 ml oil, garlic, bay. USDA FDC chicken thigh with skin (cooked) + soy sauce + vegetable oil. Assumes about half the marinade is eaten with the meat.

foods.name: Pork adobo
foods.source_note: 85 g USDA pork shoulder (cooked) + 8 g soy sauce + 5 g vinegar + 2 g vegetable oil per 100 g plated food. Sodium is soy-driven and varies.

foods.name: Sinigang na baboy
foods.source_note: Assumed 30 g cooked pork (USDA pork spare ribs, cooked) + 15 g mixed vegetables + 55 g tamarind-patis broth per 100 g. Broth-heavy plate.

foods.name: Tinola
foods.source_note: 25 g USDA chicken stewed (meat and skin) + 20 g green papaya + 55 g ginger-garlic broth per 100 g. Light soup; kcal is mostly the chicken.

foods.name: Kare-kare
foods.source_note: 40 g USDA beef oxtail (cooked) + 35 g peanut-sauce mix (USDA peanuts + rice flour + stock) + 25 g eggplant/sitaw per 100 g. Bagoong served on the side is not included in these numbers.

foods.name: Bistek Tagalog
foods.source_note: 80 g USDA beef sirloin (cooked, lean) + 10 g soy sauce + 10 g onion per 100 g. Calamansi treated like lemon juice (kcal negligible).

foods.name: Menudo
foods.source_note: USDA pork shoulder + pork liver + potato + carrot + tomato sauce, assumed 45/10/20/10/15 by cooked weight. Raisins omitted in this baseline.

foods.name: Caldereta
foods.source_note: USDA beef stew meat (cooked) + liverwurst/liver spread + potato + tomato sauce. Assumed 50/10/20/20 by cooked weight. Richer than menudo.

foods.name: Lechon kawali
foods.source_note: USDA pork belly (cooked) with extra rendered fat from deep-frying in vegetable oil. No batter. Sawsawan (vinegar-soy) not included.

foods.name: Crispy pata
foods.source_note: USDA pork leg (cooked) + skin/fat from deep-frying in vegetable oil. More meat and less pure fat than lechon kawali. Dipping sauce excluded.

foods.name: Longganisa
foods.source_note: USDA pork sausage (fresh, cooked) adjusted for a sweeter Filipino mix — added sugar from brown sugar in the cure. Garlic-heavy Lucban-style assumption, not hamonado-only.

foods.name: Tocino
foods.source_note: USDA pork fresh (cooked) plus a sugar-cure modeled as 8 g sugars / 100 g from brown sugar in the marinade. Oil uptake from frying included.

foods.name: Tapa
foods.source_note: USDA beef (top round, cooked) + soy sauce + sugar in the marinade. Oil from pan-frying included. Tapsilog garlic rice is logged separately.

foods.name: Hotdog
foods.source_note: USDA frankfurter (beef and pork) with extra starch/sugar typical of local red hotdogs. Brand variation is large — treat as a starting point.

foods.name: Daing na bangus
foods.source_note: USDA milkfish (raw) scaled to fried fish using vegetable oil uptake similar to USDA fried fish. Vinegar marinade adds little kcal; salt/soy in the daing mix drives sodium.

foods.name: Pritong galunggong
foods.source_note: USDA mackerel scad / similar small oily fish, fried in vegetable oil. Bones not eaten; numbers are edible flesh plus skin. No batter.

foods.name: Pritong tilapia
foods.source_note: USDA tilapia (cooked, dry heat) plus vegetable-oil coating from frying. No batter. Bones discarded.

foods.name: Lumpiang shanghai
foods.source_note: Filling: USDA ground pork (cooked) + carrot + onion. Wrapper: USDA egg-roll wrapper. Deep-fried in vegetable oil; oil uptake estimated.

foods.name: Pancit canton
foods.source_note: USDA egg noodles (cooked) + vegetable oil + small amounts of chicken or pork + cabbage/carrot. Soy sauce for sodium. Dry pancit, not soup.

foods.name: Pancit bihon
foods.source_note: USDA rice noodles (cooked) + vegetable oil + cabbage/carrot + soy sauce. Less protein than canton because rice noodles and less meat.

foods.name: Palabok
foods.source_note: USDA rice noodles + shrimp + pork + hard-cooked egg + a little fried pork rinds on top. Sauce thickened with rice flour / cornstarch.

foods.name: Sisig
foods.source_note: USDA pork (cooked, fatty cuts) + onion. Mayo and egg versions vary; this baseline is chopped pork with onion and a little oil, no mayo.

foods.name: Dinuguan
foods.source_note: USDA pork (cooked) + pork blood (USDA blood sausage used only as a nutrient stand-in for blood, not as a sausage) + vinegar. Puto on the side is a separate food.

foods.name: Bicol express
foods.source_note: USDA pork (cooked) + canned coconut milk + chili peppers. Bagoong contributes sodium. Coconut cream versions will run higher in fat.

foods.name: Laing
foods.source_note: USDA taro leaves (cooked) + coconut milk. Little or no meat in this baseline; pork bits would raise protein and fat.

foods.name: Ginisang monggo
foods.source_note: USDA mung beans (boiled) + vegetable oil saute + a small amount of USDA pork. Malunggay leaves add micronutrients, little kcal.

foods.name: Chopsuey
foods.source_note: USDA mixed vegetables (cabbage, carrot, cauliflower) + a small amount of chicken or pork + vegetable oil + soy-cornstarch sauce.

foods.name: Pinakbet
foods.source_note: USDA eggplant, bitter gourd, okra, squash, yardlong bean + bagoong (modeled with USDA fish sauce for sodium) + a little pork fat/oil.

foods.name: Ampalaya con carne
foods.source_note: USDA bitter melon (cooked) + beef sirloin (cooked) + vegetable oil + soy sauce. 50/40/10 vegetable/beef/sauce by plated weight.

foods.name: Fried egg
foods.source_note: USDA FDC "Egg, whole, cooked, fried". Oil amount varies by pan.

foods.name: Itlog na maalat
foods.source_note: USDA duck egg (whole, cooked) with sodium raised for a brine-cured egg. Tomato on the side is a separate food. High sodium is expected.

foods.name: Tokwa't baboy
foods.source_note: 50 g USDA tofu (firm, cooked) + 40 g USDA pork (cooked) + 10 g vinegar-soy dressing per 100 g. Frying oil on the tokwa included.

foods.name: Halo-halo
foods.source_note: Weighted mix of USDA shaved ice (water), evaporated milk, sweetened beans, jackfruit in syrup, and a small leche flan piece. Ice dilutes kcal; shop versions vary a lot.

foods.name: Turon
foods.source_note: USDA banana (raw, slightly higher solids for saba) + lumpia wrapper (USDA egg-roll wrapper) + brown sugar + vegetable oil from frying.

foods.name: Banana cue
foods.source_note: USDA banana + brown sugar coating + vegetable oil uptake from deep frying. Two saba per stick is a common street serving.

foods.name: Pandesal
foods.source_note: USDA "Rolls, hamburger or hot dog, plain" scaled to a 40 g bakery piece. Local bakeries differ; confirm against a specific store.

foods.name: Taho
foods.source_note: USDA tofu (silken) + brown-sugar syrup + cooked tapioca pearls (USDA tapioca, pearl, cooked). Syrup amount is the main swing factor.

foods.name: Champorado
foods.source_note: USDA glutinous rice (cooked) + unsweetened cocoa (stand-in for tablea) + sugar + a splash of whole milk. Tuyo on the side is a separate food.
